paper.title: Distributed Contextual Linear Bandits with Minimax Optimal Communication Cost

settings.name_in_paper: Distributed contextual linear bandits with stochastic contexts (central server, known context distribution)
unmapped: N agents communicate through a central server; communication cost (number of communicated real numbers / bits) is a second performance measure
decision set of K feature vectors drawn i.i.d. from a known distribution D per agent per round
settings.definition_quote: We consider a network of $N$ agents acting cooperatively to efficiently solve a $K$-armed stochastic linear bandit problem... each agent $i$ is given a decision set $\Xc_t^i=\{\x^i_{t,a}:a\in[K]\}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, drawn independently from a distribution $\Dc_t^i$... Assumption 1: $\norm{\boldsymbol\theta_\ast}_2\leq 1$, $\norm{\x^i_{t,a}}_2\leq 1$, $\abs{y_t^i}\leq 1$... Also, the distribution $\Dc$ is known to the agents.

settings.name_in_paper: Distributed contextual linear bandits with stochastic contexts (lower bound)
unmapped: communication budget between agents: expected number of communicated bits less than dN/64
settings.definition_quote: We consider a bandit instance where $K=2$ and the decision sets are drawn uniformly from $\left\{(\e_1,\e_2),(\e_3,\e_4),\ldots,(\e_{d-1},\e_d)\right\}$. Let $\Theta = \{\thetab\in\mathbb{R}^d:(\thetab_{2j-1},\thetab_{2j})\in\{(\Delta,0), (-\Delta,0)\}\}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian two-armed Gaussian bandit with side information
unmapped: learner has access to a side-information message M with mutual information I(M; a_*) <= 1/16
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mub_1 = (\Delta, 0)$ and $\mub_2 = (-\Delta, 0)$ and consider the Bayesian two-armed Gaussian bandit with mean $\mub$ uniformly sampled from $\{\mub_1, \mub_2\}$... Suppose additionally that the learner has access to a random element $M$ with $I(M; a_\star) \leq 1/16$.

settings.name_in_paper: Distributed contextual linear bandits with estimated context distribution (central server)
unmapped: N agents communicate through a central server
context distribution not known exactly; each agent has an estimate of the design matrix Lambda_m^i within multiplicative error eps_m
settings.definition_quote: we relax this assumption and consider more realistic settings where each agent $i$ can estimate matrix $\Lambda_m^i$ in batch $m$ up to an $\epsilon_m$ error, i.e., $(1-\epsilon_m)\Lambda_m^i\preceq\tilde \Lambda_m^i\preceq (1+\epsilon_m)\Lambda_m^i$

settings.name_in_paper: Decentralized contextual linear bandits over a communication graph (no server)
unmapped: agents are nodes of an undirected connected graph and communicate only with immediate neighbours
the learner knows the communication matrix P and its second-largest eigenvalue magnitude |lambda_2|
settings.definition_quote: In this environment, the agents are represented by the nodes of an undirected and connected graph $G$. Each agent $i$ can send and receive messages only to and from its immediate neighbors $j\in\Nc(i)$... We assume that $\mathbf{P}$ is known to the agents.

conditions: any algorithm with expected communication cost (measured in bits) less than dN/64
hard instance: K=2, decision sets uniform over {(e_1,e_2),...,(e_{d-1},e_d)}, Gaussian rewards, Delta = (1/8) sqrt(d/T)

source.label: thm:lowerbound
source.quote: Let $T\geq 4d\log(8)$. For any algorithm with expected communication cost (measured in bits) less than $\frac{dN}{64}$, there exists a contextual linear bandit instance with stochastic contexts, for which the algorithm's regret is $\Omega(N\sqrt{dT})$.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit constant BR_T >= N sqrt(dT)/2500 via Bayesian regret and Yao's principle. Main point is a communication lower bound: algorithms with < dN/64 bits suffer regret Omega(N sqrt(dT)) (vs optimal sqrt(dNT)).

conditions: side information M with I(M; a_*) <= 1/16 (also holds for sequential messages, Remark 1)

source.label: lemm:singleagentlowerbound
source.quote: Let $\mub_1 = (\Delta, 0)$ and $\mub_2 = (-\Delta, 0)$ and consider the Bayesian two-armed Gaussian bandit ... Suppose additionally that the learner has access to a random element $M$ with $I(M; a_\star) \leq 1/16$. Then, for any policy $\pi$, BR_T(\pi)\geq \Delta T\left(\frac{1}{2}-\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{16}+4T\Delta^2\right)}\right)

results.notes: Auxiliary lemma used for Theorem 1; Delta here is the half-gap parameter (gap is 2*Delta).

bound.regime: T >= Omega(d^22 log^2(NT/delta) log^2 d log^2(d/lam))

conditions: T >= Omega(d^22 log^2(NT/delta) log^2 d log^2(d lam^-1))

source.label: thm:regretandCCfpe
source.quote: Fix $M = 1+\log\left(\log\left(NT/d\right)/2+1\right)$ in Algorithm 1. Suppose Assumption 1 holds. If $T\geq \Omega\left(d^{22}\log^2(NT/\delta)\log^2 d\log^2(d\la^{-1})\right)$, then with probability at least $1-2\delta$, it holds that $R_T\leq\Oc\left(\sqrt{dNT\log d \log^2\left(KNT/\delta\la\right)}\log\log\left(NT/d\right)\right)$, and Communication Cost $\leq \Oc\left( dN\log\log\left(NT/d\right)\right)$

results.notes: R_T is defined as an expectation of regret through means but the theorem states it holds w.p. >= 1-2delta; recorded as high-probability. Regret summed over N agents. Remark 2: bit-rounded variant has same regret.

bound.regime: T >= Omega(d^22 log^2(NT/delta) log^2 d log^2(d/lam))

conditions: communication cost measured as number of real numbers communicated

source.label: thm:regretandCCfpe
source.quote: and $\text{Communication Cost}\leq \Oc\left( dN\log\log\left(NT/d\right)\right)$, where the communication cost is measured by the number of real numbers communicated by the agents.

results.notes: Communication cost bound (deterministic: dNM). Remark 2: in bits, O(dN loglog(NT/d) log(dNT)) for a rounded variant.

bound.regime: T >= Omega(d^22 log^2(NT/delta) log^2 d log^2(d/lam))

conditions: (1-eps_m) Lambda_m^i <= tilde Lambda_m^i <= (1+eps_m) Lambda_m^i with eps_m <= sqrt(lam/(N T_m))

source.label: thm:regretandCCfperelaxed
source.quote: Fix $M = 1+\log\left(\log\left(NT/d\right)/2+1\right)$. Under the setting of Lemma 4, if $T\geq \Omega\left(d^{22}\log^2(NT/\delta)\log^2 d\log^2(d\la^{-1})\right)$ and $\beta = \max_{m\in[M]}\beta_m$, then with probability at least $1-2\delta$, it holds that $R_T\leq\Oc\left(\frac{1}{1-\max_{m\in[M]}\epsilon_m}\sqrt{dNT\log d \log^2\left(\frac{KNT}{\delta\la}\right)}\log\log\left(\frac{NT}{d}\right)\right)$

results.notes: Communication cost unchanged per Remark 3. The algorithm needs estimates tilde Lambda rather than exact D.
